problems.title: A basic tangent equation
problems.question: Solve 4sin x=5cos x.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: cos x cannot be zero in this equation; divide by it.
steps: tan x=5/4. Tangent repeats every π, giving x=arctan(5/4)+kπ.

problems.title: Principal inverse-trigonometric values
problems.question: Evaluate cos(arcsin(1/3))−arctan(−√3)+arccot√3.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: arcsin lies in [−π/2,π/2]; arctan in (−π/2,π/2); use arccot in (0,π).

problems.title: Separate the variables in a trigonometric system
problems.question: Solve sin x+cos y=1/3, sin x−cos y=1/2.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
steps: 2sin x=5/6, so sin x=5/12. Also 2cos y=−1/6, so cos y=−1/12.
The sine equation gives x=(−1)ᵏarcsin(5/12)+kπ. The cosine equation gives y=±arccos(−1/12)+2mπ. The integer indices are independent.

problems.title: A prescribed amplitude
problems.question: The maximum of sin2x+a cos2x is 2. Find a.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Maximum of A sin t+B cos t is √(A²+B²).
steps: √(1+a²)=2 gives a²=3, so a=±√3. Both amplitudes are attained.

problems.title: A radical times a cosine
problems.question: Solve cos(πx)√(−x²−x+6)=0.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
steps: The radical vanishes at −3,2. Cosine vanishes at x=k+1/2. In the domain these are −5/2,−3/2,−1/2,1/2,3/2.
Take the union of both sets.

problems.title: A sum of nonnegative terms
problems.question: Find all triples satisfying x²+(y−1)²+sin z+1=0 and 2x+y+2z=1+11π.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: All three terms in the first sum are nonnegative.
steps: Each must vanish: x=0,y=1,sin z=−1. The second equation then gives 2z=11π.
z=11π/2 does have sine −1. Thus the triple is unique.

problems.title: Lateral area of a box from its diagonal inclination
problems.question: A rectangular box has base sides 12,16. Its space diagonal makes 45° with the base. Find lateral surface area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
steps: The base diagonal is √(144+256)=20, so height is 20. Base perimeter is 56.

problems.title: Surface area from three box diagonals
problems.question: A rectangular box has space diagonal 7 and lateral-face diagonals 2√6,√33 cm. Find total surface area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: For base sides a,b and height h: a²+b²+h²=49,a²+h²=24,b²+h²=33.
steps: Adding the last two and subtracting the first gives h²=8. Thus a²=16,b²=25, so edges are 4,5,2√2.

problems.title: Height of a rhombohedron
problems.question: A parallelepiped has congruent rhombus faces of side 2√2 and acute angle 60°. Find its height.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: With equal edge length s and pairwise acute representative angles 60°, the Gram determinant is s⁶/2; volume=s³/√2.
steps: Its base rhombus area is s²sin60°=s²√3/2. Divide the volume by the base area to obtain h=s√(2/3).
For s=2√2, h=4/√3. Choosing the complementary edge orientations does not change the volume or height.

problems.title: Perpendicular skew lines fix a triangular prism height
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has equilateral base side 8. Lines AB₁ and CA₁ are perpendicular. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Use A=(0,0,0),B=(8,0,0),C=(4,4√3,0), with top height h.
steps: Directions AB₁=(8,0,h), CA₁=(−4,−4√3,h) have dot product −32+h². Perpendicularity gives h=4√2.
Base perimeter is 24; lateral area is 24×4√2=96√2.
